source_documents.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission (AIE)-Active Fluorescent Probes with Multi-Binding Sites toward ATP Sensing and the Live Cell Imaging

reference_evidence_units.quote: It was also well know that AIE-active materials are sensitive to the changes of environmental viscosity, which is reasonably due to the restriction of intramolecular rotations (RIR), blocking the non-radiative pathway and opening up the 22 radiative channel.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPA-PP series
reference_evidence_units.statement: AIE and ATP turn-on attributed to RIR.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Argued for the series and TPA-PPA-3; no viscosity test for TPA-PPA-2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The emission study of probes in different solvents indicated that the fluorescence property is greatly affected by the solvent polarity, which is probably due to the intramolecular 18 charge transfer (ICT) property.
